As EP Rinkside's Sean Shapiro posted, "Dylan Larkin won't play tonight. Todd McLellan says Shawn Horcoff will address that situation."

If he goes, Detroit loses a player whose results trail his chances. Larkin has two goals in 10 games so far this season against about three expected goals (the number a player should score given the quality of his shots), a gap of about one goal. His 21.69 minutes a game are heavy, and at 5-on-5 the Red Wings generate 56.3% of the expected goals with him on the ice. The team's share of the shot quality is about 2.6 percentage points better when he plays. DET sits at 5-4-3 with 13 points and a 52.3% share of expected goals, so the underlying game is decent, but the team is 8 goals below expected. Losing a 34-goal scorer from last season won't help that. For fantasy, his value depends on where he lands, and a goal total running behind his chances argues for patience.

The team is 5-4-3 with 51 percent of the expected goals overall, so this is an average club, and a two-game absence for a third-liner shouldn't shift that much. Going by how the coach has used his players, Tyson Kozak, who plays 12:16 a night, is next in line for those minutes.

For Dallas, the move says little about the team's strength. The Stars are 7-4-1 with 15 points through 12 games, and our numbers like how they're playing. They've taken 53.7% of the expected goals so far this season (expected goals measure the quality of chances, so that's a share of the better looks), and 54% at five-on-five. Their special teams hold up too: the power play generates 0.68 expected goals per game, and the penalty kill allows 0.56.

The split between results and process is the more interesting part. Dallas has scored 4.6 fewer goals than its chances would suggest, which points to some finishing bad luck, while goalies have saved 7.6 more goals than expected given the shots they faced. That has covered for the finishing. If the shooting evens out, this team should look even better than its record.

Per Daily Faceoff, the Wild have claimed defenseman Cameron Crotty off waivers from the Senators. He played three games for Ottawa this year without recording a point.

The numbers say this is a depth move, not a needle-mover. Crotty averaged just over 11 minutes a game for OTT so far this season, and at five-on-five his team had 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances, not just the shot count) while he was on the ice. The Senators were slightly better with him off it, though three games is far too small a sample to read much into. He was drafted 82nd overall by the Coyotes in 2017, and his last AHL season, 13 points in 64 games for Tucson in 2022-23, translates to about 8 points over an NHL season by our estimate. Minnesota doesn't need much from him. The Wild sit 9-3-2 and control 59% of expected goals, and their 7.8 goals saved above expected shows how much their goaltending has helped. A third-pair option who can hold even is all they're asking for.

Daily Faceoff's Tyler Yaremchuk and Carter Hutton called Jarry's shutout against the Flames a hopeful sign for the Oilers, and said Edmonton needs that kind of goaltending right now.

Our numbers explain the urgency. EDM is 9-2-2, but goals saved above expected, which measures how many goals a goalie or team stops compared with what the quality of shots against would predict, sits at minus 6.4 so far this season. That means the Oilers have given up about six more goals than the chances warranted. The record has been carried by scoring: EDM has put in 15.2 more goals than its chances would predict, and its share of expected goals, the quality of chances taken versus allowed, is only 52.8 percent overall and 49 percent at five-on-five. A team living on finishing luck with shaky goaltending is fragile, so one shutout matters less than whether the saves keep coming.

CGY's side shows how close the margin is. The Flames are 5-7-0 with a 46.7 percent expected goals share and are 6.6 goals short of expectation at scoring, so their results trail their play slightly. Edmonton would benefit most if Jarry steadies the minus 6.4.

A team creating good looks but not finishing them can always use proven shooters nearby, and 40 goals in 70 AHL games is exactly that profile. A tryout carries no promise of an NHL call-up, so we'd treat this as depth, not a lineup change. If MIN's finishing stays cold, though, the pool of scorers in Iowa is worth watching.

Without him, that picture could change quickly.

Bobrovsky's .885 save percentage looks ugly, but his goals saved above expected is +0.92 in 10 games, so he has been a bit better than the shots he's faced. That's a far cry from last season's -13.5 over 52 games. We'd call this a slow start with some luck-adjusted support, not proof the decline is over.

In the 5 games since he went out, Lars Eller has taken his spot beside Reinhart and Tkachuk, rising to 16:07 a night from 13:16, and Bokondji Imama has gone to 8:32 from 5:40. Florida has controlled 56% of the quality of chances at five-on-five this season, and with Barkov on the ice that share was 75% over two games.

items.text: Activated C/RW Benjamin Kindel from injured reserve. Placed C/LW David Gustafsson on waivers.
Assigned D Charles Alexis Legault to Chicago (AHL).
Assigned D Ryan Ufko to Milwaukee (AHL).
Loaned D Hoyt Stanley to Belleville (AHL).
Placed F Dylan Larkin on the non-roster injured reserve.

moves.take: Detroit announced it has placed forward Dylan Larkin on the non-roster injured reserve. Larkin has played 6 games this season with 1 goal and 3 points, after scoring 34 goals last year, and he averages 21.81 minutes a night. Going by how the coach has used his players, Viktor Arvidsson (19:15 a night) is next in line for those minutes, and Michael Rasmussen, the busiest man on the second power-play unit, is the likeliest to move up. Detroit is 3-3-2 and has generated about half the expected goals so far (49.8%).

items.text: Loaned D Dennis Gilbert to Rochester (AHL).
Placed D Ivan Provorov on injured reserve.
Signed D Tristan Luneau to a six-year contract extension.
Assigned F Rutger McGroarty to Wilkes-Barre/Scranton (AHL).
Placed G Joonas Korpisalo on injured reserve. Recalled G Dylan Garand from Hartford (AHL).
Placed F Matt Duchene on long-term injured reserve retroactive to Sept. 29. Recalled Fs Arttu Hyry and Colin Blackwell from Texas (AHL).

moves.take: Dallas announced it placed forward Matt Duchene on long-term injured reserve, retroactive to Sept. 29, and recalled forwards Arttu Hyry and Colin Blackwell from Texas (AHL). Hyry, who kills penalties on the third line, has three goals this season, about 1.2 more than his chances would predict, and Dallas controls more of the chance quality when he plays at even strength. Blackwell has gone without a point and the team has done worse with him on the ice. Going by how the coach has used his players, Oskar Bäck is next in line for Duchene's minutes.

items.text: Placed F Ryan Nugent-Hopkins on injured reserve. Placed D Alec Regula on long-term injured reserve. Recalled F Josh Samanski under emergency conditions.

moves.take: EDM announced it placed Ryan Nugent-Hopkins on injured reserve, placed Alec Regula on long-term injured reserve and recalled Josh Samanski under emergency conditions. Nugent-Hopkins has played 19.95 minutes a night, mostly on the second line and the first power-play unit, so Owen Michaels (12:49 a night) is next in line for his minutes and Kasperi Kapanen is the likeliest to move up on the power play. Samanski has averaged 7.73 minutes in six games, so this is a much smaller role. The Oilers are 8-2-1, and their even-strength expected goal share is 49%.

items.text: Recalled D Dennis Gilbert from Rochester (AHL). Placed G Alex Lyon and D Olen Zellweger on injured reserve. Signed D Louis Crevier to a four-year contract. Transferred F Matthew Savoie to long-term injured reserve.
Signed C William Karlsson to a two-year contract.

Reassigned C Roger McQueen and C Cruz Lucius to San Diego (AHL). Recalled D Noah Warren, D Ian Mitchell and D Tristan Luneau from San Diego. Placed D Drew Helleson on injured reserve. Moved RW Troy Terry from the non-roster list to long-term injured reserve.

moves.take: Anaheim announced it reassigned centers Roger McQueen and Cruz Lucius to San Diego (AHL), recalled defensemen Noah Warren, Ian Mitchell and Tristan Luneau, placed Drew Helleson on injured reserve, and moved Troy Terry to long-term injured reserve. Helleson's minutes should go to Tyson Hinds and Pavel Mintyukov, who are both playing more in the one game since he went out. Luneau, a top-pair defenseman at 19:28 a night, comes back with Anaheim holding 54.6% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) at five-on-five while he plays.

items.text: Moved C Max Domi from the non-roster list to long-term injured reserve.
Reinstated C Blake Lizotte from injured reserve.

moves.take: Pittsburgh announced it has reinstated center Blake Lizotte from injured reserve. Lizotte, a third-line forward who plays 13:08 a night and kills penalties, has no goals and four assists in 11 games, and the Penguins have controlled 61 percent of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) with him on the ice at five-on-five. Pittsburgh's team share improves by about 10 percentage points when he plays. His return should take minutes back from Hendrix Lapierre, who is next in line at 11:11 a night.

items.text: Signed G Casey DeSmith to a two-year contract.
Placed G Cayden Primeau on waivers.
